title: fusion-pipeline internal
description: Overview (throughput, latency, backlog, failures, CPU, memory), one row per stage, Internals collapsed. Spec: docs/specs/2026-09-08-observability-pipeline-poc.md, Telemetry.

options.content:
**How to read this board** — every chart has history; hover for the exact value, the legend shows *Last / Max / Mean* for the window, widen the time range top-right for more.  
**Healthy:** *in* ≈ *out*, *errored* flat at 0, *waiting in NATS* flat, *end-to-end p99* under the dashed 1 s line.  
**Something wrong?** *Is anything failing?* names the node → open its **Stage** row below. Slow? *slowest stage p99* names it → its *Time per record*. Costly? *What does it cost?*. Filter by **Tenant** / **Stage** top-left.  
**One record:** *Explore* → **Loki**, `{service_name="fusion-pipeline"} | record_id="<id>"`, shows its stage errors, naks, redeliveries and dead letters; *Open trace* on a line shows its spans in **Tempo**. The tenant view is the *fusion-pipeline tenant* board.

panels.title: Are records flowing?  (in → out, dropped, errored)
panels.description: in: records the source handed to the engine. out: sink writes with durable acceptance (PubAck). dropped: on purpose, see Drops by reason. errored: failed in a stage or a sink; each one naks its message.

panels.title: How slow?  (end to end, and the slowest stage)
panels.description: End-to-end: the record's ingestion time to settlement. Slowest stage p99: the worst stage run or sink PubAck wait right now; find which in the per-stage rows below. Rule of thumb: watch above 1 s, problem above 5 s. Gaps are minutes with no records: latency is undefined without them; the grey bars show how many records the number is based on.

panels.title: Is NATS backing up?  (waiting, in flight, redelivered)
panels.description: Waiting grows when the pipeline is slower than the producer. In flight is what the workers hold. Redelivered means naks or lost acks. Rule of thumb: watch above 100, problem above 1000.

panels.title: Is anything failing?  (errors, naks, redeliveries)
panels.description: Flat at zero is healthy. errored counts a stage error or a sink without PubAck once, under its node; pipeline headers ignored counts a Fusion-* header the source could not parse (the message is still walked); each failed record naks; JetStream redelivers up to max_deliver, and a record that fails its last delivery is dead-lettered to dlq.{tenant} and terminated. dead-letter publish failed: the last delivery could not reach the DLQ either; the message is left in its stream (see the stream sequence in the pipeline log). Internals shows dead letters by stage and reason.

panels.title: What does it cost?  CPU (cores)
panels.description: Cores in use, self-reported. Pipeline: one line per instance from process.cpu.time. NATS: varz cpu. Dragonfly does not export CPU.

panels.title: What does it cost?  memory (RSS)
panels.description: Resident memory, self-reported: pipeline process.memory.usage per instance, NATS varz mem, Dragonfly used_memory_rss.

panels.title: Source (NATS in)  —  what the engine did before any stage ran
Handed over → entered the graph → rejected
panels.description: Every record the source handed to the engine; those with an id and of kind log entered the first stage; the rest were rejected here (missing_id naks and comes back, invalid_record acks and is gone).

panels.title: Stage: $stage  —  records, time per record, why records left, state store
Records in / out
panels.description: What this node did with its records. For source: intake and the engine's own drops. For a sink: out means PubAck.

panels.title: Time per record (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Stage run time, or for a sink the wait for durable acceptance (PubAck). Includes any state-store round trip the stage makes. Gaps are minutes with no records: latency is undefined without them; the grey bars show how many records the number is based on.

defaults.noValue: no records through this node in this window

panels.title: Why records left here
panels.description: Drop reasons are the spec's closed set. Errored and no-PubAck are failures, not drops.

panels.title: Dragonfly calls (state store)
panels.description: Dragonfly round trips this stage makes: ops/s, p99 per op, and errors/s (the store unreachable or timing out; what happens to the record then is the node's on_state_error). Empty for stages without state.

defaults.noValue: no state ops from this stage

panels.title: Edit ops that could not apply (by op, field, cause)
panels.description: edit_unapplied_total for this stage: ops/s whose source read as null (cause=absent) or whose target refused the value (cause=type). Under on_unapplied: skip this is the only sign the node is not doing its job; under drop the same records show in "Why records left here" as edit_unapplied. Empty for stages that are not edit nodes.

defaults.noValue: no unapplied ops from this stage

panels.title: Coverage  —  the last loghub-check run, with or without chaos (make chaos)
Did every record arrive?  (reached converging to expected; published, received)
panels.description: The loghub verifier's judgement, exported every 5s while a run goes on and once more when it is final (settled = 1). expected: (line, subject) pairs the run must deliver, a Linux line counting on main and audit and a sampled-out line on neither main nor, outside Linux, anywhere. reached: those some copy of the line reached; while records are in flight it trails expected, and on a run without loss it meets it, also after the chaos run's kill and pause. published: messages the producer got a PubAck for. received: distinct (record, subject) pairs read back, duplicates that got through included. sampled out: lines the sample node leaves off the main subject. The series go stale 5 minutes after the run.

panels.title: Is anything lost?  (missing, unexpected, dead-lettered, wrongly written; extra copies)
panels.description: missing: a line's duplicate group has not reached a subject it should (in flight while the run goes on; 0 once settled on a pass). unexpected: a record nobody published, on a subject it never reaches, or under the wrong tenant. dead-lettered: a published record in DLQ. edit / lua mismatch: a main-subject record without what those nodes write. A run passes when these are 0 at settled = 1 and dedupe dropped at least 80% of the planned duplicates. extra copies: a second copy on one subject, which at-least-once delivery allows. repeated on every subject: a fan-out record copied twice on each of its sinks, which a kill between them leaves (a dedupe race does too).

panels.title: Extraction mismatch by format  (lines whose attributes differ from the structured CSV)
panels.description: Per log format, the duplicate groups whose extracted attributes differ from the line's row in the loghub structured CSV, compared on the main sink. Reported, never gated: a mismatch is a finding about the pattern. The verifier prints the mismatching LineIds.

panels.title: How well does each pattern extract?  (share of lines matching the structured CSV)
panels.description: Per log format, the share of duplicate groups whose extracted attributes equal the line's row in the loghub structured CSV, compared on the main sink. Reported, never gated: a mismatch is a finding about the pattern. The verifier prints the mismatching LineIds.

panels.title: Intake per instance
panels.description: One line per pipeline process. After a restart the old instance goes stale and a new one appears; the Overview sums them.

panels.title: Busy workers
panels.description: Worker time inside stages and sink writes, in whole workers; compare with the configured worker count.

panels.title: Lua errors by kind
panels.description: lua_errors_total by kind, every lua node summed: instructions (budget tripped), memory (cap tripped), runtime (the script raised), output (the returned record was refused). What happened to those records is the node's on_error: pass forwards them, drop shows them under lua_error in the stage rows, nak shows them as errors. The compose pipeline's split_lines node runs with pass.

panels.title: Regex limit trips and non-matches
panels.description: Drops with reason regex_limit (match, depth, heap, work or input-size limit tripped) and records a regex node's pattern did not match, per node and engine.

panels.title: Dragonfly server
panels.description: Server side of the state store, from its own /metrics.

panels.title: Pipeline process threads
panels.description: Threads per instance: workers, source, NATS I/O, exporter. A steady climb is a leak.

panels.title: Dead letters by stage and reason
panels.description: dlq_total by the node that failed (source: before any node ran) and the kind of failure: stage_error, state_error, sink_error, panic (dev builds only), missing_id, undecodable. Each is a message that failed every delivery, now on dlq.{tenant} with a Fusion-Dlq-Reason header, and terminated.

panels.title: Dead-letter publish time (p50 / p99)
panels.description: dlq_publish_duration_seconds: one dead letter from the first publish to its PubAck or the last failed retry, retries included. This long, a worker (or, for an undecodable payload, the source) was held on a message's last delivery.

panels.title: Bytes in / written per sink
panels.description: bytes_in_total: payload bytes as received, rejected records included. bytes_out_total: bytes each sink wrote with durable acceptance; a fan-out counts every copy.
